text: dsh-pijul 为 DSH 接入 Pijul 分布式版本控制工具，通过 shell 服务在会话工作目录中调用 Pijul 命令。它提供仓库状态与差异查看、变更记录和查询、通道与远端管理，以及克隆、拉取和推送等能力，并将命令结果整理为成功状态、退出码和标准输出或错误。适合在 DSH 对话中管理 Pijul 仓库的开发者。运行需要本机安装 Pijul；记录变更还需要 SSH agent 和 Pijul signing identity。

dsh-pijul adds Pijul tools to DSH through the session shell. Inspect status and diffs, record and review changes, manage channels and remotes, and clone, pull, or push repositories. Pijul must be installed locally; recording needs an SSH agent and signing identity.
想在 DSH 对话里查看 Pijul 仓库状态和未记录的差异。
怎么从聊天中记录变更并查看某次提交的内容？
I want to pull or push Pijul changes from my DSH session.
dsh-pijul 的功能「检查与记录变更」：可查看仓库状态、日志和未记录差异，并按消息记录变更或查看指定变更详情；通过 DSH 工具调用并返回命令结果。
dsh-pijul 的功能「同步与组织仓库」：可克隆仓库、推送或拉取变更，并管理远端和通道；用户通过对应工具提供远端、通道或变更参数。
dsh-pijul 使用本机 SSH agent 中的密钥为 Pijul 记录签名；插件默认将 SSH_AUTH_SOCK 指向 ~/.ssh/agent.sock，记录操作需要可用的签名 identity。

dsh-pijul README · What changes after installing：The agent gains sixteen tools that drive the `pijul` CLI through the harness `shell` service, under the calling session's standing sandbox policy and working directory:

dsh-pijul README · What changes after installing：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pijul_status` | Working-copy state: current channel, unrecorded changes, untracked files |
| `pijul_log` | Recorded changes, newest first (`limit`, `offset`) |
| `pijul_diff` | Unrecorded changes as hunks, optionally limited to paths |
| `pijul_init` | Create a repository |
| `pijul_clone` | Clone from a URL, SSH target or local path |
| `pijul_add` | Start tracking paths (`recursive` to include directory contents) |
| `pijul_record` | Record a change with a message, non-interactively |
| `pijul_change` | Show one change by hash or unambiguous prefix |
| `pijul_unrecord` | Drop changes from the current channel — Pijul's undo |
| `pijul_reset` | Discard unrecorded working-copy changes |
| `pijul_push` | Push to a remote (`--all` by default) |
| `pijul_pull` | Pull from a remote (`--all` by default) |
| `pijul_remote` | List remotes, set the default, delete one |
| `pijul_channel` | List, create, switch, delete or fork channels |
| `pijul_apply` | Apply recorded changes to the current channel |
| `pijul_identity` | List the signing identities pijul knows about |

dsh-pijul README · What changes after installing：Every tool returns `{ ok, exitCode, timedOut, aborted, stdout, stderr }`, and renders as a compact `[tool] ok/failed` block. `repo` defaults to the session working directory, so inside a repository chat you can omit it.

dsh-pijul README · Requirements：- **Pijul 1.0.0-beta.x on `PATH`** (tested against `1.0.0-beta.21`), e.g. `cargo install pijul --version 1.0.0-beta.21`. An absolute path can be pinned instead through the plugin's `binary` config key.
- **An SSH agent holding a signing key, plus a pijul identity.** pijul 1.0-beta signs every recorded change with a key from the agent. One-time setup:

dsh-pijul README · Requirements：```sh
  ssh-agent -a ~/.ssh/agent.sock      # persistent agent; the plugin defaults SSH_AUTH_SOCK here
  ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519           # your signing key
  pijul identity list                 # an identity already exists? done.
  pijul identity new default --no-link --display-name "You" --email you@example.com

dsh-pijul README · Requirements：Every command runs under `SSH_AUTH_SOCK="${SSH_AUTH_SOCK:-$HOME/.ssh/agent.sock}"`, so a persistent agent at that socket keeps recording working across harness restarts. Diagnose failures with `pijul_identity`.

dsh-pijul README · Install：From GitHub — the repository is plain ESM with no build step, so a git install needs **no `prepare` script and no build allowance**:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:erkinalp/dsh-pijul
```

Pin a commit if you want the code you audited to be the code that runs:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:erkinalp/dsh-pijul#<commit-sha>
```

From a local checkout or a packed tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-pijul
```
dsh-pijul README · Install：Restart `dsh web` (or the profile's process) afterwards. Confirm the layer landed with `dsh --profile web --dump-config` — it shows a `# == dsh-pijul` block.

[agent] pijul_init  {path: "notebook"}                      → ok

        pijul_record{repo: "notebook", message: "initial import",

dsh-pijul README · Non-interactivity：A pijul command that opens an editor does not just fail an agent — it blocks the tool until the shell timeout. The plugin is built so that cannot happen, and the two cases it must defend against were found by probing `1.0.0-beta.21`:

dsh-pijul README · Non-interactivity：| pijul behaviour | How the plugin handles it |
| --- | --- |
| `pijul record <paths> -m <msg>` opens the commit-message editor **even though `-m` was given** (in every flag order) | The command preamble exports `EDITOR`/`VISUAL` as the shell builtin `true`, a no-op. pijul then accepts the template it already wrote — the `-m` message — instead of waiting on an editor. |
| `pijul push` / `pijul pull` without `--all` open the editor to pick changes | `--all` is the default, and the same no-op editor makes the explicit `all: false` escape hatch safe rather than hanging. |
| `pijul unrecord` with no hashes shows an interactive selection | `pijul_unrecord` requires at least one hash. |
| `pijul add .` records only the directory itself, **not its contents** | `pijul_add` exposes `recursive` (pijul `--recursive`); the tool description says so, because "add everything" is the common intent. |
dsh-pijul README · Non-interactivity：The plugin never prompts, and it never leaves a process attached to a terminal.

dsh-pijul README · Permissions and compatibility：- **Permissions**: commands run through the harness `shell` service under the calling session's standing sandbox policy — the same confinement as the built-in `bash` tool. Repositories are read and written under the session workspace; the SSH agent is used only to sign recorded changes. The plugin makes no network calls of its own: `pijul clone`/`push`/`pull` reach the network only when you invoke them.
- **External services**: none. Fully offline for local repositories.
- **Compatibility**: DeepSeek Harness profiles built on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` (DSH `>=0.2.0 <0.3.0`). It uses `tools`, `shell` and `systemPrompt`, and reads `sandboxPolicy`, `shellEnv` and `workingDirectory` when the profile provides them. pijul `1.0.0-beta.x`.
- **HTTPS remotes** support clone and pull but not push; use SSH or a local path to push.

dsh-pijul README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `pijul binary not found on PATH` | Install pijul, or set `config.binary` to an absolute path on the `pijul` row. |
| `pijul_record` fails with an SSH or identity error | Recording is signed. Run `pijul_identity`; start the agent at `~/.ssh/agent.sock` and `ssh-add` your key (see [Requirements](#requirements)). |
| `Error: Already in a Pijul repository` | `pijul_init` on a directory that already holds a repository. That is a pijul error with exit 1, not a no-op. |
| `Refusing to reset, as there are unrecorded changes` | `pijul_reset` first, or record them, before switching channels. |
| A tool reports `sandbox: file access denied` | The session's sandbox policy governs the repository path; widen the workspace or move the repository inside it. |

dsh-pijul README · Troubleshooting：On some systems the distro/snap `pijul` package cannot run inside a container because it hard-codes an `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` under a read-only `/run`; a plain binary (`cargo install` or a release tarball) is the reliable choice.

dsh-pijul README · Development：Plain ESM, no build step, **zero dependencies**: `index.mjs` has no imports and exports `name`, `inject` and `apply(ctx, config)` per the [DeepSeek Harness plugin spec](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Tool definitions are plain objects with hand-converted JSON Schema, so `ctx.tools.register` accepts them without `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`.

dsh-pijul README · Development：That is deliberate. A pnpm-linked bundle's bare imports resolve from the checkout's real path rather than the profile's `node_modules` and can be pruned by a later `dsh plugin add`; a dependency-free plugin can never fail to import.

```sh
npm test              # unit + integration (node:test, no install step)
npm run test:unit     # 34 tests, no pijul required
npm run test:integration   # drives the real pijul CLI; self-skips when absent
```

dsh-pijul README · Development：The unit tests build the plugin against a stub that mirrors the real service shapes — `ctx.tools.register`, `ctx.systemPrompt.section`, `ctx.shell.resolve` → `ctx.shell.execute` → `result()`, and `ctx.get` for optional services — so a regression in the shell seam fails here rather than in a chat. The integration tests run the exact command strings the plugin produces, in a real `bash`, against a real repository.

dsh-pijul README · Development：The bundle manifest lives in `package.json` (`dsh.bundle` → `cordis.patch.yml`), which inserts the `pijul` row into the profile composition. The `binary` config key is read as a plain value from the row config:

```yaml
- id: pijul
  name: dsh-pijul
  config:
    binary: /usr/local/bin/pijul
